    AI Overview
    League of Legends (LoL) is a popular free-to-play, 5v5 team-based MOBA developed by Riot Games for Windows and macOS, focusing on destroying the enemy team's base (Nexus). Players choose from over 170 unique champions—ranging from tanks and mages to assassins—and compete in tactical, 30-minute matches. 
    Getting Started & Gameplay 
    • Sign Up: Create an account on the official website to download the Riot Client.
    • Objective: Work with four teammates to destroy the enemy's Nexus while defending your own.
    • Roles & Champions: Select from 170+ champions across five main roles: Top Lane, Jungle, Mid Lane, Attack Damage Carry (ADC), and Support.
    • Progression: Level up during the match, earn gold, and purchase items to make your champion stronger. 
    Platforms & Technical Requirements 
    • Platforms: PC (Windows) and Mac (macOS).
    • System Requirements: The game is designed to run on a wide range of hardware, generally requiring a modern processor (Intel Core i3-530 or AMD A6-3650), at least 2GB of RAM (4GB or more is recommended), and a decent graphics card (NVIDIA GeForce 9600GT or AMD HD 6570), with roughly 16GB of free disk space.
    • Controls: The game uses a standard keyboard and mouse layout, with default display settings changeable via the video menu or Alt + Enter. 
    Key Game Modes 
    • Summoner's Rift: The main 5v5 competitive map.
    • Howling Abyss (ARAM): A single-lane, fast-paced battle mode.
    • Teamfight Tactics (TFT): An auto-battler game mode located within the same client. 
    You can learn more about the game's mechanics, champions, and lore on the League of Legends homepage.

    League of Legends, commonly referred to as League, is a multiplayer online battle arena video game developed and published by Riot Games. Inspired by Defense of the Ancients, a custom map for Warcraft III, Riot's founders sought to develop a stand-alone game in the same genre.
